title: Lorry Licence Categories: C1, C, C1+E, C+E
whatItIs: Your lorry licence category depends on the vehicle's maximum authorised mass (MAM) and the trailer. C1 is for medium lorries, C for large ones. Add +E for a trailer over 750 kg.
keyFacts: To drive a type of vehicle, you need an 'entitlement' for that category on your driving licence.
C1: vehicles between 3,500 and 7,500 kg MAM, with a trailer up to 750 kg.
C1+E: a C1 vehicle with a trailer over 750 kg. The combined MAM can't exceed 12,000 kg.
C: vehicles over 3,500 kg MAM, with a trailer up to 750 kg.
C+E: a category C vehicle with a trailer over 750 kg.
An articulated lorry needs category C+E, and you must take your test in one.

notes: Older names: a category C licence may be known as 'HGV 2', and towing heavier trailers as 'HGV 1'.

b.label: C (large lorry)

onTheTest.question: You hold category C1 on your licence. What is the heaviest vehicle (MAM) you can drive?
onTheTest.why: Category C1 covers vehicles between 3,500 and 7,500 kg maximum authorised mass, with a trailer up to 750 kg.

onTheTest.question: Which licence category do you need to drive an articulated lorry?
onTheTest.why: GOV.UK gives an articulated lorry as a category C+E vehicle, and says you must use an articulated lorry for the test.

traps: '+E' is about the trailer: a trailer over 750 kg needs +E; one up to 750 kg doesn't.
C1+E is capped at 12,000 kg combined MAM. C1 alone stops at 7,500 kg.
Upgrading from C to C+E: no new provisional licence or part 1 test, but you must pass parts 3a and 3b.
Applying for a provisional C licence also gives you provisional C1, C1+E and C+E.
